identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir yanda karakter, dayanıklılık ve cömertliği; öte yanda büyüklük duygusu, gurur, onur, yüksek amaç ve kendine saygıyı aktarır. Dal korunabilir, ancak bu iki görünüm tek ve ayrışmaz bir huy gibi sunulmamalıdır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: sağlam karakterli, dayanıklı ve cömert adam
büyüklük duygusu, onur, yüksek amaç ve kendine saygı

lexicalization_scope.note: Kişiyle kurulan kalıp karakter, dayanıklılık ve cömertliği; çıplak biçim büyüklük, onur ve yüksek amacı bildirir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün aday kartlar karşılaştırıldı; cömertlik ortaklığı ile karakter gücü ve eylem hevesi ayrımını gösteren komşu seçildi.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak kişinin yerleşik karakter gücü ve özdeğerini anlatır; komşu ise iyilik yapma anındaki gönüllü canlılık ve atılganlığı öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, dayanıklılık ve cömertliğin yanında gurur, onur ve yüksek amacı da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, iyilik yapmaya hevesle yönelme, canlılık ve gönül genişliği üzerinde durur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal, cömert ve iyi davranışa yatkın kişi görünümünde örtüşür.

branches.source_phrase_ar: رجل له نفس أي خلق وجلادة وسخاء (ayn); النفس العظمة والكبر والعزة والهمة والأنفة (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak kaydı, sağlam ve cömert karakter görünümünü kişinin büyüklük, onur, yüksek amaç ve kendine saygı duygularıyla yan yana getirir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى الخلق والجلادة والسخاء، وبمعنى العظمة والكبر والعزة والهمة والأنفة.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو النفيس من المال ولا المنافسة على شيء خارج النفس.

concept_gloss.applicability: Mekânsal aralık, nesne boyutu, ek süre veya bir işteki hareket alanı anlatıldığında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Mekânı, boyutu, süreyi ve hareket alanını ortak genişleme ölçüsüyle korur.

concept_map.definition: Yer bakımından uzaklık veya aralık, boyut bakımından uzunluk ve genişlik, zaman ya da iş bakımından ise ek süre ve hareket alanıdır. Bütün kullanımlarda sınırlar arasındaki payın büyümesi esastır.

facets.statement: Mekânda iki sınır arasındaki uzaklık, açıklık veya boyutsal genişliktir.
Zamanda ek süre, işte ise rahat davranmaya elveren hareket alanıdır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir işi yapmak için yeterli serbestlik ve ek zaman bulunduğu bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İşteki serbestliği ve ek süre payını birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.text: rahat hareket edecek alan ve süre

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal ölçülebilir yer, boyut veya süre genişliğidir; belirli bir sıkıntıyı giderme ya da sabahın açılması değildir.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi mekânsal uzaklık ve genişliği, işte hareket alanı ve süre payını, ayrıca uzunluk ve zaman uzatımını aynı genişleme ölçüsü altında açıkça toplar.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: ek süre ya da hareket alanı
daha uzak, daha uzun ya da daha geniş

lexicalization_scope.note: Kalıp kullanım bir işteki hareket alanını, biçimler ise süre payı ile mekânsal ya da boyutsal genişliği anlatır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; uzunluk ve uzaklık ortaklığının yanında odaktaki süre ve hareket alanı ekini gösteren komşu yayımlandı.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal genişleyen payı yer, boyut ve süre arasında geneller; komşu dal belirli varlıkların uzun veya uzak oluşuna ve işin uzamasına yönelir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, uzaklık ve uzunluğun yanında ek süreyi ve bir işteki rahat hareket alanını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, uzun insanı, uçsuz bucaksız yeri ve uzun süren işleri özel kullanımlar olarak kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal mekânsal uzaklık, uzunluk ve bir işin sürmesi alanında örtüşür.

branches.source_phrase_ar: هذا المكان أنفس من ذاك أي أبعد شيئا (ayn); أنت في نفس من أمرك أي في سعة ولك في هذا الأمر نفسة أي مهلة (sihah); هذا المنزل أنفس أي أبعد وكتبت كتابا نفسا أي طويلا وزد في أجلي نفسا وبين الفريقين نفس أي متسع (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar uzaklık, açıklık, uzunluk, ek süre ve işte hareket alanını sınırlar arasındaki payın genişlemesi altında birleştirir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه السعة في الأمر، والفسحة، والمهلة، وطول الأجل أو النهار أو الكتاب، وبعد المنزل واتساع ما بين الفريقين.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو تفريج الكربة المخصوص ولا تنفس الصبح من حيث الانفلاق إلا إن كان المراد مطلق الامتداد.

concept_gloss.applicability: Belirli oyun okunun baskın aktarımdaki sırası ve pay değeri kastedildiğinde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Oyun alanını, belirli oku, beşinci sırayı ve beş payı korur.

concept_gloss.text: eski bahis oyunundaki beşinci pay oku

concept_map.definition: Eski bir bahis oyununda kullanılan, çoğunluk aktarımına göre beşinci sıradaki ve beş pay taşıyan oktur. Başka bir aktarım onu dördüncü sıraya koyar.

facets.statement: Eski bahis oyunundaki beşinci pay oku olarak ve beş payla tanımlanır.
Aynı toplu kaynak kaydında okun dördüncü sırada olduğu yönünde karşı bir aktarım bulunur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sıra konusundaki karşı aktarım özellikle belirtilirken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Belirli oyun okunu ve dördüncü sıra karşı aktarımını korur.

contextual_glosses.text: dördüncü sayıldığı da aktarılan oyun oku

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Adlandırma eski bahis oyunundaki belirli oka aittir; temel sıra beşinci, kayıtlı karşı görüş dördüncüdür.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin baskın bildirimi, belirli bahis okunun beşinci sırada olduğu ve beş pay taşıdığı yönündedir. Aynı toplu iddiada dördüncü sıra biçiminde bir aktarım da bulunduğu için sıra tartışmasız gösterilemez.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: eski bahis oyunundaki beşinci pay oku; bir aktarıma göre dördüncü ok

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak biçim yalnızca eski bahis oyunundaki belirli pay okunu adlandırır; kişi ya da değer yarışması anlamı taşımaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün aday kartlar değerlendirildi; genel oyun oku komşusu, özel sıra ve pay değerinin dalı nasıl daralttığını en açık biçimde gösterir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal sıra ve pay değeriyle belirlenen özel oktur; komşu dal ise herhangi bir oyun okunu veya işlenmemiş ok gövdesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, belirli sıraya ve beş pay değerine sahip tek bir oyun okunu adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: oyun oku ve çıplak ok gövdesi
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, henüz uç ve tüy takılmamış ok gövdesini ve oyun oklarının herhangi birini genel olarak kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da eski bahis oyununda kullanılan ok biçimli araç alanında kesişir.

branches.source_phrase_ar: النافس الخامس من القداح (ayn); النافس الخامس من سهام الميسر ويقال هو الرابع (sihah); النافس الخامس من قداح الميسر وفيه خمسة فروض (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak kaydı belirli oyun okunu çoğunlukla beşinci sıra ve beş payla tanımlar; bunun yanında dördüncü sıra aktarımını da korur.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه النافس اسما لقدح من قداح الميسر، خاصة الخامس على نص أكثر المصادر، مع التنبيه إلى قول الرابع في Sihah.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو العائن ولا المتنافس في القيمة.

root_profile.summary: Kök, soluk alıp vermeden sıkıntı giderme, kan, doğum, içim payı, su, açılma-genişleme, değer yarışı, canlılık, özdeşlik, iç düşünce, karakter ve eski oyun okuna uzanan çok dallı bir anlam ağı kurar. Dalların bir bölümü soluk ve yaşam çevresinde gevşekçe bağlanırken bir bölümü kalıba bağlı uzmanlaşmış adlandırmalardır.

text.arabic_uthmani: وَكَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيهَآ أَنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ بِٱلنَّفْسِ وَٱلْعَيْنَ بِٱلْعَيْنِ وَٱلْأَنفَ بِٱلْأَنفِ وَٱلْأُذُنَ بِٱلْأُذُنِ وَٱلسِّنَّ بِٱلسِّنِّ وَٱلْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌۭ ۚ فَمَن تَصَدَّقَ بِهِۦ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌۭ لَّهُۥ ۚ وَمَن لَّمْ يَحْكُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

baseline.text: Tevrat'ta onlara cana can, göze göz, buruna burun, kulağa kulak, dişe diş ve yaralara karşılık yazdık. Kim bu hakkından vazgeçerse bu, kendisi için bir arınma olur. Allah'ın indirdiğiyle hükmetmeyenler zalimlerin kendileridir.

findings.text: Kısas, yaranın açtığı izi aynı ölçüyle izleyerek karşılık verir.
Hakkından vazgeçmek, yaralanma izinin ilerlemesini durdurur ve vazgeçen için koruyucu bir örtü olur.

activation_trace.role: The identity or very self of the thing supplies the matched unit on both sides of the first pair.
The literal seeing organ makes the correspondence concrete rather than merely monetary or abstract.
Equivalence between injury and response names the list's governing proportional mechanism.

changed_reading.after: The catalogue is also a ceiling: response is confined to a precisely corresponding life, organ, or wound.
changed_reading.before: The verse is a catalogue authorizing bodily retaliation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated X-bi-X pairs at words 5-14 culminate in qisas at word 16.
baseline_models.mechanism: Each injured life or organ is paired with its counterpart, while qisas names equivalence of the injury; the list therefore fixes a correspondence that limits the response as well as authorizing it.

activation_trace.role: Charitable transfer, including yielding one's due, turns the enforceable claim into a gift.
Effacing sin by covering it gives the waived claim a consequence beyond simple non-enforcement.

changed_reading.after: The measured legal claim itself can be donated, and its donation performs a covering act without the verse resolving whether lahu points to donor or offender.
changed_reading.before: Pardon is optional leniency appended to an otherwise complete sanction.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The conditional at words 17-23 turns the qisas claim into something that can be given away and calls the result kaffara.
baseline_models.mechanism: The right-holder may treat the exact claim as a charitable right and relinquish it; that relinquishment covers or effaces culpability for the beneficiary left grammatically open by lahu.

activation_trace.role: An inscription that establishes an obligating judgment makes the bodily correspondences an entrusted norm.
Restraint that repels corruption supplies judgment's protective function.
Putting something in its proper station frames revelation as an order delivered for fitting enactment.
Withholding and confining a right identifies the concrete harm produced by refusing the delivered judgment.

changed_reading.after: Not judging actively traps another's due and defeats the norm's function of restraining injury.
changed_reading.before: Not judging is generic disobedience to a command.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse moves from what was written upon them in it to judging by what God sent down, and names refusal zulm.
baseline_models.mechanism: A fixed, delivered norm must be enacted through judgment that restrains wrong; failure is not passive omission but withholding a due and dislocating the entrusted order.

activation_trace.role: Matched injury remains the focus verse's immediate legal mechanism.
A life-bearing self is the single unit whose taking is expanded to a collective scale.
Wholeness without remainder supplies the all-people horizon on both the killing and preserving sides.
Preserving life by refraining from killing supplies the positive end toward which proportional restraint points.

changed_reading.after: Life-for-life is a bounded response designed against the collective multiplication of a single killing, with preservation rather than exchange as its wider horizon.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier inscription scales one unlawfully taken life to all people and one preserved life to all people. That scale changes the one-for-one rule from private exchange into a restraint whose horizon is preservation of the whole human field.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies single-life equivalence, collective scaling, and preservation; I add the arrow that a fixed one-for-one ceiling blocks violence from multiplying through the collective. A live alternative is that 5:32 supplies only a moral preface and does not define qisas's social function.
structural_cues: 5:32 repeats the written-upon-them construction and the phrase nafs bi-ghayri nafs before 5:45 repeats nafs bi-nafs.
The killing-all and preserving-all clauses place both destructive escalation and life-preserving interruption around the same single life.

activation_trace.role: Yielding a due as charity supplies the focus verse's voluntary off-ramp.
Covering the offense's residue names the off-ramp's restorative consequence.
Covering a wrong while protecting its bearer supplies an exit immediately after the severe sanctions of 5:33.
Tender mercy prevents the sanction unit from closing on punishment alone.
Removing estrangement between people makes reform relational repair after the theft sanction.

changed_reading.after: The pardon clause is the focus instance of a repeated sanction-to-repair design: accountability establishes the claim, then return, repair, or voluntary release can interrupt its terminal enforcement.
changed_reading.before: The pardon clause is a private exception after the rule.

context_deltas.mechanism: Two surrounding sanction units immediately open into forgiveness, mercy, or repair. The same sequence recurs inside 5:45 when exact sanction opens into donated claim and covering, making the off-ramp part of the legal architecture rather than an ornamental exception.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies three penalty-to-release adjacencies and branch images of covering, mercy, and reconciliation; I infer a repeated legal design in which liability remains real but need not be the sequence's endpoint. The live alternative is that the three off-ramps are offense-specific provisions with no shared architecture.
structural_cues: The sanction of 5:33 is followed by the pre-capture exception of 5:34.
The theft sanction of 5:38 is followed by repentance and repair in 5:39.
The bodily correspondences in 5:45 are followed within the same ayah by donation and kaffara.

activation_trace.role: Corrective restraint supplies the action that blocks manipulation from becoming judgment.
Putting something in a materially wrong place supplies the focus condemnation's spatial logic.
Tilting away from a direction gives the manipulation of legal words its operative motion.
A settled placement supplies the position from which the words are being diverted.
The straight balance supplies the counter-mechanism for judging the competing parties.

changed_reading.after: Judging by revelation means resisting outcome-shopping, keeping words in their assigned relations, and measuring the claim straightly; selective displacement is itself the zulm.
changed_reading.before: Judging by revelation means selecting and imposing the stated penalty.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context depicts corruption as tilting words away after their placements and contrasts it with judgment on a straight measure. This spatializes the focus verdict: hukm restrains selective displacement, while zulm is the resulting misplacement or detention of a right.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies directional deviation, settled places, a straight balance, and focus zulm; I infer that faithful judgment restores legal words and claims to their fitting places. A live alternative is that the placement language concerns textual alteration only and should not govern the proportional list.
structural_cues: 5:41 couples displacement of words with verdict-shopping: take this outcome, beware if it is not given.
5:42 permits declining jurisdiction but requires qist if judgment is undertaken.
5:45's exact bodily correspondences occur inside this dispute over manipulated judgment.

activation_trace.role: Covering or denying truth supplies one way the delivered judgment is defeated.
Confining a right supplies the focus verse's distinct injury-centered diagnosis.
Something exiting its casing supplies a boundary-breaking diagnosis for the repeated failure.

changed_reading.after: At the center of the three formulas, zalimun highlights the rights-level effect of failed judgment: a due is withheld or put out of place, alongside truth-covering and boundary-exit.
changed_reading.before: Zalimun is a generic condemnation equivalent to the neighboring labels.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same non-judgment formula receives three adjacent predicates. Their branch images allow complementary failure modes: covering truth in 5:44, withholding or displacing a right in 5:45, and breaking out of a containing boundary in 5:47.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies one repeated formula and three branch-distinct labels; I treat them as layered diagnostics of one refusal rather than interchangeable insults. A live alternative is that the labels are rhetorically cumulative or synonymous and do not partition mechanisms.
structural_cues: 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47 repeat the same whoever-does-not-judge-by-what-God-sent formula.
The focus verse occupies the middle of the Torah, bodily-rights, and Gospel sequence.

activation_trace.role: Donation of a right supplies the concrete focus act.
Making a prior promise or claim true in action supplies the immediate confirming echo.
A second confirmation recurrence stabilizes the link between truth and enacted continuity.

changed_reading.after: Voluntary waiver can carry the law's truth through in another mode: the established claim is given, and that truthful act produces covering rather than counter-injury.
changed_reading.before: Mercy relaxes justice by declining to carry the law through.

context_deltas.mechanism: The root used for giving away the qisas claim recurs immediately for active confirmation of prior revelation. The echo permits waiver to be read not as suspending truth but as one way the law's truth is made effective.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an unusually dense shared-root recurrence across donation and confirmation; I infer a semantic echo in which relinquishing the claim can verify rather than negate the law's purpose. A live alternative is that charity and confirmation remain separate established senses with no functional bridge.
structural_cues: The focus act of tasaddaqa is followed in 5:46 by two occurrences of musaddiqan.
5:48 again describes the newly sent book as musaddiqan in the same revelation-and-judgment sequence.

activation_trace.role: An obligating inscription anchors the focus rule while its upon-them/in-it grammar specifies its entrusted setting.
Putting a norm in its fitting station allows delivery to include situated application.
Witnessing guardianship supplies the new book's accountable relation to what precedes it.
Making something take a state supplies both the differentiated paths and the unrealized one-community alternative.
An open approach to a water source gives each community's shir'a a concrete route of access.
A plainly marked road supplies the distinct minhaj paired with that access route.
Advancing in competition supplies the commanded movement across differentiated paths.
Beneficial good supplies the competition's common direction rather than legal sameness.

changed_reading.after: The focus rule is a real obligation entrusted to a named community in its scripture; the surrounding sequence preserves accountability while recognizing differentiated revelatory routes and a common test in doing good.
changed_reading.before: What God sent down denotes a single decontextualized legal code whose faithful use is identical everywhere.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus grammar assigns a rule to them within it; the later book both guards prior witness and situates communities in made paths before directing competition toward goods. Judging what was sent down is thus entrusted enactment within a specified revelatory relation, not automatic flattening into one undifferentiated code.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies specified pronouns, successive entrusted scriptures, differentiated routes, and a shared race toward goods; I infer that fidelity is covenant-situated while still answerable to revealed truth. A live alternative is that the plurality concerns secondary rites only and leaves the focus sanction uniformly transferable.
structural_cues: 5:44 identifies Torah as the delivered medium, 5:45 says written upon them in it, and 5:47 addresses the people of the Gospel.
5:48 explicitly contrasts made law-and-way plurality with the unrealized possibility of one community and then commands racing in good.

remaining_uncertainties: The antecedent and beneficiary of lahu in the kaffara clause remain grammatically unresolved.
The sadaqa/tasdiq bridge may be a deliberate functional echo or only a dense recurrence of distinct root senses.
The kafirun-zalimun-fasiqun sequence may encode layered mechanisms, rhetorical accumulation, or substantial overlap.
The scope of law-and-way plurality in 5:48 may not determine how broadly the focus sanction transfers.
strongest_changes: The one-for-one rule became a collective life-preservation ceiling rather than a private exchange formula.
The donation clause became the third instance of a repeated sanction-to-repair architecture.
Failed judgment became spatial and procedural: words are tilted from their places, the measure is bent, and a right is withheld.
summary.what_was_special: The packet made the focus verse function as a hinge: it looks backward to the single killing scaled to all life and repeated repair off-ramps, while looking forward to displaced legal words, layered non-judgment diagnoses, confirming scriptures, and differentiated entrusted paths.

activation_trace.role: Following a trace step by step supplies an evidentiary or measured undertone within the focus term.
Equivalent counter-injury keeps the exploratory trace reading bounded by the term's direct legal sense.
Following after a trace immediately after the focus verse activates qisas's trace branch.
A remaining mark that evidences what occurred supplies the object that disciplined response follows.

changed_reading.after: Secondarily, qisas can sound like a response disciplined by the injury's trace: establish and follow the actual mark closely enough that equivalence does not become projection or excess.
changed_reading.before: Qisas means only reproducing the injury on the offender.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because qisas's direct injury-equivalence branch is explicit and must remain primary. It remains anchored in the same focus root's trace-following branch and is activated by the immediate qaffa/athar sequence in 5:46. Downstream prose should present it only as a secondary lexical resonance: retaliation must track the actual injury or precedent, not replace qisas with narrative succession.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Qisas at 5:45 word 16 carries both injury-equivalence and following-a-trace branches.

activation_trace.role: Eyewitness observation supplies one channel by which a judgment can know an injury.
Listening that accepts what is heard supplies the vulnerable reception channel.
Impeaching a witness or tongue lets bodily wounds resonate with damaged testimony.
Opening the mouth in speech supplies the context's professing-but-unbelieving output channel.
Hearing as understanding and compliance turns repeated lie-listening into corrupted uptake.
Falsehood supplies the content that deforms the listening-and-testimony chain.

changed_reading.after: Without ceasing to be literal, the eye-ear-wound sequence also shadows the evidentiary body of judgment: seeing, receptive hearing, and credible testimony can themselves be damaged by a market for false verdicts.
changed_reading.before: The anatomical list concerns only matched physical losses.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is cross-domain and surprising because the listed organs are literal objects of injury. It remains anchored in focus branches for seeing, receptive hearing, and impeaching testimony, activated by 5:41's mouths, lie-listening, and falsehood. Downstream prose must retain bodily qisas as primary and qualify this only as an epistemic shadow cast by the surrounding corrupted-hearing dispute.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus inventory permits the eye as seeing, the ear as receptive hearing, and jarh as impeaching a witness or tongue.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Retaliation follows the wound's exact trace.** `ق ص ص B001` is following a trace and `B003` equivalent retaliation; the body-part repetitions make equivalence visible. I infer that law retraces injury to prevent punishment from wandering beyond it.
2. **Relinquished right covers its holder.** `ص د ق B006` is charity/relinquished right and `ك ف ر B009` covering or effacing sin. The victim can interrupt equivalence by donation. I infer that surrendering the claim transforms an outward deficit into inward covering without denying the original wound (`ج ر ح B001`).
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Retaliation follows the injury’s trace exactly, but relinquishment can stop the trace.** Fixed **ق ص ص / B001** (“following a trace”) and **B003** (“equivalent retaliation”) explain the repeated organ-for-organ mapping. Fixed **ص د ق / B006** (“charity and relinquished right”) then offers a branch where the injured claimant releases that mapped response. I infer that *taṣaddaqa bihi* interrupts the otherwise authorized following of harm with a voluntary cession that covers liability. The ayah reads as exact traceability with a built-in stopping mechanism, not as an unqualified cycle of mirroring.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:46’s trace-following revelation placed organ-for-organ *qiṣāṣ* inside a larger textual succession, and 5:47–5:50 kept its application answerable to revealed judgment.

words.gloss_range: coordinating continuation into the cited Torah statute
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as continuation, not as an isolated new maxim. It carries the prior Torah scene (5:44) into a more specific legal disclosure, so the statute moves from guarded scripture and judges to the actual content written upon the community.

topics.headline: opening continuation into statute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not begin as a hard reset; it carries the prior Torah discourse into a specific written prescription.
topics.reason: The opening coordinator resumes the 5:44 Torah scene and launches the legal content of 5:45 as continuation.

words.gloss_range: completed divine writing or ordaining of the following legal content
words.prose: {{ar:كَتَبْنَا}} ({{tr:katabna}}), with {{ar:ك ت ب}} ({{tr:k-t-b}}), makes the retaliation list a completed divine inscription and prescription. The following content clause is not detached: life, organs, wounds, mercy, and warning all sit under the act of writing. The root's joining pressure also makes the ordinance bind obligation to consequence, and the 5:32 echo keeps this as part of the surah's written life-law field.
words.root_gloss_range: writing, inscription, ordaining, and joining; locally a completed divine prescription binding the following equivalence law

topics.headline: completed divine prescription governs the list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the body-part chain as inscribed legal content under a completed divine act, not as a loose proverb.
topics.reason: The perfect first-plural verb governs the following content clause; k-t-b rows add inscription, ordaining, and binding imagery, with 5:32 as a concrete life-law parallel.

words.gloss_range: upon them, marking imposed obligation on the prior Torah-facing community
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:alayhim}}) places the written prescription upon its recipients. The preposition marks burden rather than benefit, and the plural suffix keeps the prior Torah-facing community in view before the verse locates the rule in scripture.

topics.headline: obligation laid on named recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the statute is placed upon the prior community rather than floated as an unlocated maxim.
topics.reason: The preposition plus plural suffix marks burden and imports the prior Torah addressees before the scripture locator appears.

words.gloss_range: in it, referring to the Torah as textual container
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَآ}} ({{tr:fiha}}) locates the prescription inside the prior feminine scriptural referent from 5:44. The wording separates the people on whom the duty is imposed from the Torah in which the rule resides.

topics.headline: scriptural container for the prescription
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the law as located inside the Torah, with source and addressee kept grammatically distinct.
topics.reason: The fī phrase with feminine suffix refers back to the Torah in 5:44 and places the cited rule inside that textual container.

words.gloss_range: assertive content particle introducing the written legal clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) turns the following body-part sequence into asserted written content through the qisas predicate. The standard reading keeps the list under one governed accusative clause, letting the noun-for-noun units function as binding law even without a repeated retaliation verb; variant nominatives show a real structural pressure toward independent equations without displacing the local parse.

topics.headline: assertive content clause houses the list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one asserted clause holds the whole equivalence series, while variant readings expose but do not replace the standard governed structure.
topics.reason: The standard mushaddad particle governs the accusative list; accepted variants show an independent-equation pressure but remain apparatus for the local standard surface.

words.gloss_range: legal person or life, with self, breath, soul, and blood pressure retained
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّفْسَ}} ({{tr:al-nafsa}}), with {{ar:ن ف س}} ({{tr:n-f-s}}), opens the equivalence chain as the first accusative term under anna at the level of whole person-life. Its definiteness and singularity make the legal unit bounded, while the root range keeps breath, blood, self, and embodied life underneath the juridical term.
words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, life, breath, person, appetite, and blood; locally whole person-life as the first legal unit

topics.headline: whole person starts the cascade
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the statute begin with the whole life-person before descending into particular organs and wounds.
topics.reason: The first definite singular accusative under the content clause carries the n-f-s range of person, life, self, breath, and blood, and anchors the later body cascade.

words.gloss_range: bāʾ of equivalence or exchange in the first X-for-X pair
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) establishes the statute's exchange relation. Here the particle is locally narrowed to equivalence, so the second life term becomes the matched answer to the first and the same relation can be reused through the list.

topics.headline: first exchange bāʾ establishes the formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exact requital is carried by the short preposition that will repeat across the organ list.
topics.reason: Local repetition fixes bāʾ as equivalence or exchange rather than generic instrument, and this first instance establishes the series mechanism.

words.gloss_range: matched genitive person-life term governed by the exchange preposition
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّفْسِ}} ({{tr:al-nafsi}}), with {{ar:ن ف س}} ({{tr:n-f-s}}), completes the first mirror pair. The same definite life term returns under the preposition, so the equivalence is heard as matched person-life against person-life rather than as an abstract compensation scale.
words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, life, breath, person, appetite, and blood; locally the same whole person-life repeated as the equivalent side

topics.headline: second life term completes the mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the life-for-life pair as exact repetition with a case shift, not a loose value comparison.
topics.reason: The genitive after bāʾ repeats the same definite singular n-f-s field on the exchange side.

words.gloss_range: coordinator introducing the next matched body-part unit
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes the eye a new coordinated legal unit. The repeated connector keeps the body-part series countable and ordered, with each item applying the same matching rule.

topics.headline: connector adds the eye as a new unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the list step forward item by item instead of collapsing the eye into the first life clause.
topics.reason: The conjunction before the eye coordinates a new legal item and preserves the ordered cascade.

words.gloss_range: the eye as a definite singular organ of sight, with source and perception range in the background
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَيْنَ}} ({{tr:al-ayna}}), with {{ar:ع ي ن}} ({{tr:'-y-n}}), moves the law from whole life to the first named organ of perception. The local word is the eye, while the root range lets sight feel like a source-point of direct perception; variant case readings only qualify the syntax, not the selected organ sense.
words.root_gloss_range: eye, spring, source, essence, and direct perception; locally the definite organ of sight in the matched injury list

topics.headline: eye as governed perception organ
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first specific organ is sight, with source and direct-perception pressure retained under the legal sense.
topics.reason: The local sense is the concrete eye, but the root range of source, spring, essence, and seeing enriches the organ term; nominative variants expose a case boundary without replacing the standard accusative.

words.gloss_range: repeated bāʾ of equivalence before the eye counterpart
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) repeats the exchange governor for the eye pair. The grammar does not invent a new relation for sight; it ports the same X-for-X mechanism onto a new organ, and the bound recitation makes preposition and organ arrive as one compact exchange phrase.

topics.headline: exchange frame repeats for the eye
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relation stays mechanically identical while the body part changes.
topics.reason: The second bāʾ reuses the equivalence governor, making the eye pair inherit the same legal syntax as the life pair.

words.gloss_range: the matched genitive eye governed by the exchange preposition
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَيْنِ}} ({{tr:al-ayni}}), with {{ar:ع ي ن}} ({{tr:'-y-n}}), answers the first eye with the same definite organ. The case changes under the preposition, but the root and article repeat, making the equivalence visibly exact.
words.root_gloss_range: eye, spring, source, essence, and direct perception; locally the equivalent eye in the second half of the pair

topics.headline: matched eye completes the pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second eye repeat the same organ and root under genitive case, preserving exact correspondence.
topics.reason: The genitive definite singular repeats the same eye/source field as the accusative term and completes the surface mirror.

words.gloss_range: coordinator introducing the nose as the next legal item
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the body-part chain moving after the eye. It adds the nose as another parallel unit and prevents the list from ending before the remaining organs and wounds appear.

topics.headline: connector sustains the cascade
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the sequence continue after the eye pair instead of closing early.
topics.reason: The mid-list conjunction adds the nose and preserves the parallel legal cascade.

words.gloss_range: the definite singular nose as a prominent facial organ in the equivalence list
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَنفَ}} ({{tr:al-anfa}}), with {{ar:أ ن ف}} ({{tr:'-n-f}}), names the projecting organ of the face. The legal sense is the nose, but the front-edge and honor field make the injury more than a generic nasal category; variant case readings only mark the syntactic pressure around the list.
words.root_gloss_range: nose, forefront, beginning, projection, and pride or disdain; locally the physical nose as a marked legal unit

topics.headline: rare nose term as prominent matched organ
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the nose is not a routine inventory item; its rarity and front-pride field make this small organ conspicuous.
topics.reason: The local sense is the physical nose, while root and rarity rows preserve forefront, projection, and honor pressure; variants expose case pressure but do not replace the standard governed term.

words.gloss_range: bāʾ of equivalence before the nose counterpart
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) binds the rare nose term to the same exchange relation. The preposition makes the pair legally ordinary even while the organ itself remains lexically marked, and its recitational fusion makes the exchange relation heard before the noun's rarity is fully processed.

topics.headline: same exchange frame binds the nose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rare nose term governed by the same equivalence syntax as the earlier pairs.
topics.reason: The bāʾ before the nose counterpart repeats the exchange relation and keeps the rare organ inside the common legal mold.

words.gloss_range: the matched genitive nose on the equivalent side
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَنفِ}} ({{tr:al-anfi}}), with {{ar:أ ن ف}} ({{tr:'-n-f}}), completes the rare nose mirror. The second form is not redundant; it supplies the counterpart that lets the concrete nose sense function as a full legal pair.
words.root_gloss_range: nose, forefront, beginning, projection, and pride or disdain; locally the same physical nose repeated as counterpart

topics.headline: second rare nose completes the mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rare concrete nose sense defined by its matched pair rather than by an isolated occurrence.
topics.reason: The genitive counterpart repeats the same rare concrete a-n-f lexeme and makes the nose pair corpus-defining inside the statute.

words.gloss_range: coordinator introducing the ear as the next matched organ
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the ear without changing the series logic. The same connector keeps the sensory-organ chain parallel before the final singular organ and the plural wound category arrive.

topics.headline: connector adds the hearing organ
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the eye-nose-ear sequence remain parallel before the list turns toward tooth and wounds.
topics.reason: The conjunction extends the additive legal sequence to the ear while preserving the established mold.

words.gloss_range: the definite singular ear as hearing organ, with permission and receptivity field retained
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأُذُنَ}} ({{tr:al-udhuna}}), with {{ar:أ ذ ن}} ({{tr:'-dh-n}}), gives the list its hearing organ. The legal referent is the ear, but the root family of permission, announcement, and access lets the organ register as a receptor for authorized sound; the cluster of accusative, nominative, and sukun variants makes this the variation-rich body part without changing the local sense.
words.root_gloss_range: ear, permission, announcement, call, and receptivity; locally the concrete hearing organ in the matched injury list

topics.headline: ear as receptor with permission pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ear as an organ of reception and authorized access, not merely tissue in a list.
topics.reason: The local sense is the concrete ear, while the a-dh-n family supplies hearing, permission, call, and receptivity; accepted variants expose recitational and case pressure without changing the referent.

words.gloss_range: bāʾ of equivalence before the ear counterpart
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) carries the ear into the same X-for-X frame. The hearing organ receives no special syntax; the repeated preposition keeps the law formally identical, and the compact phrase audibly binds the receptor to the exchange relation.

topics.headline: exchange frame repeats for hearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the hearing organ placed under the same legal relation as life, eye, and nose.
topics.reason: The bāʾ before the ear counterpart repeats the equivalence construction for another sensory faculty.

words.gloss_range: the matched genitive ear on the equivalent side
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأُذُنِ}} ({{tr:al-udhuni}}), with {{ar:أ ذ ن}} ({{tr:'-dh-n}}), answers the first ear with the same receiving organ. The genitive case marks the exchange side, and lighter variant pronunciations affect cadence rather than the legal match.
words.root_gloss_range: ear, permission, announcement, call, and receptivity; locally the equivalent hearing organ in the second half of the pair

topics.headline: matched ear repeats reception image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second ear keeps both the bodily match and the access-reception field, while variant sound weight remains apparatus.
topics.reason: The genitive counterpart repeats the same ear root; sukūn variants alter sound but not the governed role or organ sense.

words.gloss_range: coordinator introducing the tooth as the last singular organ pair
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the tooth as another coordinated unit. Its position sets up the last specific organ before the ayah broadens from matched parts to wounds generally.

topics.headline: connector sets up last singular organ
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees tooth introduced as the final precise organ before the statute expands to wounds.
topics.reason: The conjunction adds another parallel item and marks the transition point before the open plural injury category.

words.gloss_range: the definite singular tooth, with sharp edge and established-track pressure in the background
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسِّنَّ}} ({{tr:as-sinna}}), with {{ar:س ن ن}} ({{tr:s-n-n}}), closes the singular organ series with a sharp bounded item. The local word is the tooth, but the root range of edge, age, and established path makes the legal pair feel like an exact cutting track; variants qualify the syntax.
words.root_gloss_range: tooth, age, sharpening, edge, and established practice or path; locally the physical tooth in the matched organ list

topics.headline: tooth as edged organ under case pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the tooth as a sharp bounded organ whose root also evokes edge, age, and established path.
topics.reason: The local sense is tooth, while s-n-n rows preserve sharpening, age, and sunna-track pressure; nominative variants expose clause architecture without replacing the standard accusative.

words.gloss_range: bāʾ of equivalence before the tooth counterpart
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) applies the same exchange preposition to the tooth. The formula remains unchanged at the final singular organ, while the assimilated sound makes the pair feel especially compact.

topics.headline: exchange frame sharpens the tooth pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same equivalence relation compressed into the final specific organ pair.
topics.reason: The repeated bāʾ applies the same exchange syntax to the tooth, with assimilation and gemination rows adding recitational compression.

words.gloss_range: the matched genitive tooth completing the last specific X-for-X pair
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسِّنِّ}} ({{tr:as-sinni}}), with {{ar:س ن ن}} ({{tr:s-n-n}}), completes the tooth-for-tooth mirror. The same definite form returns under the preposition, with the doubled nūn and established-track field preserving the sharp tooth pressure as the sequence of exact singular organ matches closes before wounds broaden the scale.
words.root_gloss_range: tooth, age, sharpening, edge, and established practice or path; locally the equivalent tooth on the response side

topics.headline: second tooth closes the exact pairs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the fifth body-part pair close with the same definite root shape and only case changed.
topics.reason: The genitive counterpart repeats the definite tooth term and completes the sequence of exact singular organ mirrors.

words.gloss_range: plural wounds as the open injury category after the named organs
words.prose: {{ar:وَٱلْجُرُوحَ}} ({{tr:wa-l-juruha}}), with {{ar:ج ر ح}} ({{tr:j-r-h}}), is the widening mechanism of the statute. After life, eye, nose, ear, and tooth, the plural wound term gathers remaining bodily injuries into the rule, with the cutting-and-acquiring root field keeping liability visible. Variant case readings sharpen the pivot from list item to independent maxim.
words.root_gloss_range: wounding, cutting, gaining, and committing; locally bodily wounds that create adjudicated liability

topics.headline: plural wounds open the injury class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the list widen from five exact singular pairs into a plural catch-all for bodily injury.
topics.reason: The broken plural changes scale after the singular organs; j-r-h adds cutting, wound, and earning-liability pressure, and variant nominatives show the final clause can stand as a legal maxim.

words.gloss_range: retribution in kind or measured equivalence, especially for the wound clause
words.prose: {{ar:قِصَاصٌۭ}} ({{tr:qisasun}}), with {{ar:ق ص ص}} ({{tr:q-s-s}}), names the rule as the nominative predicate resolving the wound clause after the body-part cascade. It is not bare punishment: the root image of tracing and cutting makes requital a measured following of the injury. Its position also hinges the ayah from strict equivalence into the mercy clause, with 2:178-179 as the larger qisas background.
words.root_gloss_range: following tracks, narrating, tracing, cutting, and retaliation; locally measured legal matching that follows the injury

topics.headline: qisas names the matching rule and hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the list land on a named category of measured matching just before mercy opens.
topics.reason: The nominative predicate names the rule for wounds and summarizes the list; q-s-s rows preserve tracking and cutting imagery, and 2:178-179 anchor the legal category.

words.gloss_range: consequential pivot from equivalence law into the remission condition
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) marks the turn from strict matching into remission. Its position after qisas makes the next whoever-condition a legal branch from the rule rather than a detached reflection, with the result following immediately from the act of relinquishment.

topics.headline: fa branches from qisas to remission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is opened as a legal branch from qisas, not as an unrelated moral aside.
topics.reason: The particle immediately after qisas introduces the conditional remission clause and marks a structural turn.

words.gloss_range: conditional whoever introducing the forgiveness branch
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the mercy condition with an indefinite human actor. The pronoun lets the rule apply case by case while forming a parallel with the later warning condition.

topics.headline: whoever opens the mercy condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the mercy option made open to any relevant actor while being paired with the later warning condition.
topics.reason: The conditional relative pronoun universalizes the positive branch and participates in the paired man-conditionals of the second half.

words.gloss_range: voluntary charitable relinquishment of the retaliation claim
words.prose: {{ar:تَصَدَّقَ}} ({{tr:tasaddaqa}}), with {{ar:ص د ق}} ({{tr:s-d-q}}), transforms a retaliation right into an act of truth-charity. The Form V shape keeps the actor personally involved in relinquishment, while variant imperfect framing remains a timing note rather than a change in the local completed conditional.
words.root_gloss_range: truth, sincerity, confirmation, and charity; locally forgiving a retaliation right as enacted truth-charity

topics.headline: forgiveness as truth-charity action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that relinquishing retaliation is framed as enacted truth and charity, not mere non-enforcement.
topics.reason: Form V from s-d-q makes the waiver agent-involving and truth-charity charged; the imperfect variant usefully exposes temporal framing without changing the local perfect conditional.

words.gloss_range: by or with it, referring to the relinquished right, wound, or claim
words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) attaches the object of remission to the charity verb. The suffix can point to the retaliation right, the wound, or the whole legal claim, so the act of giving up covers both the injury and the right attached to it.

topics.headline: ambiguous object keeps right and wound live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is given up remains grammatically compact and deliberately broad: qisas, wound, or the legal claim as a whole.
topics.reason: The bāʾ plus suffix attaches the relinquished item to the charity verb; reference evidence supports a locally useful ambiguity among right, wound, and claim.

words.gloss_range: apodosis marker introducing the result of the mercy condition
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) launches the answer to the forgiveness condition. It turns the act of relinquishment into a stated legal result before the expiation noun appears.

topics.headline: fa launches the expiation result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees expiation as the direct answer to the forgiveness condition, not a detached comment.
topics.reason: The particle marks the apodosis after the forgiveness protasis and shifts from act to result.

words.gloss_range: independent pronoun in the result clause, identifying the waiver with expiation
words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) makes the result clause an explicit equation. It can point to the act of waiver and, by extension, to the one who waives, so expiation is presented as the standing identity of that relinquishment.

topics.headline: pronoun identifies act or actor with expiation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the result clause as an identity statement: the relinquishment itself, and possibly the forgiver, is linked to expiation.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun strengthens the nominal equation; referent rows preserve act-or-actor ambiguity without overfixing it.

words.gloss_range: expiation or atoning covering produced by relinquishment
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَّارَةٌۭ}} ({{tr:kaffaratun}}), with {{ar:ك ف ر}} ({{tr:k-f-r}}), is the mercy branch's landing word. The same covering root that can name denial in the warning field becomes positive here: forgiveness produces atoning covering rather than concealment of truth, a boundary reversal from 5:44.
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, denial, ingratitude, and expiation; locally positive remedial covering of sin or liability

topics.headline: kaffara reverses covering into expiation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the k-f-r root shift from negative covering in the neighboring warning field to positive covering through forgiveness.
topics.reason: The predicate is an intensive abstract noun of expiation; rows tie it to the covering root, the 5:44 boundary contrast, and the mercy branch landing point.

words.gloss_range: for him, assigning the expiation benefit to the relevant person, especially the forgiver
words.prose: {{ar:لَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) closes the mercy clause on the beneficiary. The lām makes expiation count for someone, most directly the forgiver, while the pronoun leaves enough room for the legal benefit to be read through the waiver scene.

topics.headline: benefit assigned to the forgiver
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that expiation is not only social repair; the grammar routes benefit to a personal recipient.
topics.reason: The lām plus suffix marks beneficiary most directly as the forgiver, while rows preserve limited referent openness.

words.gloss_range: coordinator linking the warning condition to the mercy condition
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links the next condition to the completed mercy clause. The conjunction makes the warning branch a paired legal outcome beside forgiveness and expiation.

topics.headline: wa pairs warning with mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second conditional joined to the first as a paired outcome, not as an unrelated ending.
topics.reason: The conjunction begins a complete second man-clause and links mercy and refusal-to-judge as complementary legal outcomes.

words.gloss_range: conditional whoever introducing the refusal-to-judge warning
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) repeats the open conditional frame, now for refusal to judge. The same structure that made mercy available to whoever waives also generalizes the warning against rejecting revealed judgment.

topics.headline: whoever opens the warning condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final warning generalizes beyond the immediate injury case while remaining parallel to the mercy option.
topics.reason: The second conditional pronoun repeats the mercy branch architecture but now governs refusal to judge by revelation.

words.gloss_range: negation particle governing the jussive judgment verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) gives the warning its clipped negative onset. It governs the following jussive verb, so refusal to judge is grammatically marked rather than left as a loose failure.

topics.headline: lam negates judgment decisively
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning is built on a grammatically decisive negation, visible in the following jussive verb.
topics.reason: The particle governs jussive mood on the judgment verb and forms part of the repeated 5:44, 5:45, 5:47 warning core.

words.gloss_range: negated jussive act of judging or governing by the revealed standard
words.prose: {{ar:يَحْكُمْ}} ({{tr:yahkum}}), with {{ar:ح ك م}} ({{tr:h-k-m}}), is the act negated in the closing warning. The jussive form shows lam's force, and the repeated formula across 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47 lets the same refusal be named by different final verdicts. The root image of restraint makes non-judgment a failure to restrain by the revealed measure.
words.root_gloss_range: judging, governing, deciding, wisdom, and restraining or bridling; locally the act of judgment negated in the warning formula

topics.headline: jussive judgment verb anchors the refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same negated judging act receive different verdict labels across 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47.
topics.reason: The verb is apocopated by lam and belongs to the repeated man-lam-yahkum formula; h-k-m rows add restraint and judgment imagery without moving away from the local refusal.

words.gloss_range: bāʾ of criterion, by or according to the revealed standard
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches the judgment verb to its criterion. The warning is measured by what was sent down, not by judgment in the abstract, and the same criterion hinge recurs in 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47.

topics.headline: bāʾ makes revelation the standard
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure is not simply lack of judgment; it is failure to judge by the revealed criterion.
topics.reason: The bāʾ in bima marks means and standard, participates in the repeated 5:44, 5:45, 5:47 refrain, and links back to the Torah-contained content cited earlier.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun meaning what, gathering revealed content as criterion
words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:ma}}) gathers the revealed content into the criterion phrase. It does not isolate one statute only; it lets the final warning move from the qisas law just cited to the revealed standard as a whole.

topics.headline: relative pronoun gathers revealed content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closing warning broaden from the cited statute to whatever God has sent down.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is governed by bāʾ and opens the revealed-content clause within the criterion phrase.

words.gloss_range: He sent down, causative revelation as completed delivered standard
words.prose: {{ar:أَنزَلَ}} ({{tr:anzala}}), with {{ar:ن ز ل}} ({{tr:n-z-l}}), defines the judgment criterion as something already sent down. The Form IV causative makes revelation a delivered standard from God, available for human judgment, and the same bima-anzala formula anchors the three warnings in 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47.
words.root_gloss_range: descending, alighting, lodging, arrival, and provision; locally caused revelation sent down as the criterion for judgment

topics.headline: caused descent makes revelation available
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices revelation as a completed divine descent made available for judgment, not a vague inspiration.
topics.reason: The perfect Form IV verb completes the relative clause and gives the criterion a causative divine-delivery frame; the phrase recurs in 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47.

words.gloss_range: Allah as the nominative agent of sending down the criterion
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allahu}}), with {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:'-l-h}}), is the named agent of the revelation verb. The ayah begins with first-person divine writing and then closes the criterion phrase with the divine name, turning disclosed law into a standing standard answerable to God.
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, and the disputed bewildered-devotion field; locally the named divine agent of revelation

topics.headline: divine name anchors the criterion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the criterion clause lands on the named revealer, so refusal answers to divine authority rather than an abstract norm.
topics.reason: The nominative divine name is the agent of the revelation verb; rows also preserve the person shift from first-plural writing to third-person named criterion.

words.gloss_range: apodosis marker introducing the verdict clause
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the refusal condition into consequence. It opens the verdict clause, so the condemnation is not free-floating but follows directly from not judging by what God sent down.

topics.headline: fa turns condition into verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the warning move directly from condition to formal verdict.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the apodosis before the distant demonstrative and makes the verdict syntactically dependent on the refusal condition.

words.gloss_range: distant plural demonstrative marking the warned group as those people
words.prose: {{ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulaika}}), with {{ar:أ و ل}} ({{tr:'-w-l}}), points the non-judging group out as those people. The demonstrative creates moral distance and begins the stable verdict frame repeated in 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47 before the final labels change.
words.root_gloss_range: demonstrative pointing and remoteness; locally a distanced subject for the verdict clause

topics.headline: distant demonstrative sets the class apart
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the non-judgers pointed out at moral distance before the final label arrives.
topics.reason: The distant plural demonstrative opens the nominal verdict and forms the stable fa-ulaika-humu frame repeated in 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47.

words.gloss_range: separating pronoun between demonstrative subject and verdict predicate
words.prose: {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) locks the demonstrative subject to the predicate. As a separating pronoun, it sharpens the identification and keeps the final clause compact, emphatic, and formulaic across 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47.

topics.headline: separating pronoun sharpens identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verdict as emphatic identification: those are precisely the wrongdoers.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun functions as a separating pronoun in the nominal verdict formula and remains stable across the triple warning.

words.gloss_range: the wrongdoers, a definite plural class identified by injustice
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ}} ({{tr:al-zalimun}}), with {{ar:ظ ل م}} ({{tr:z-l-m}}), seals the ayah by naming non-judgment as wrongdoing. The definite active participle turns the conditional violators into a recognized class, and the root's wrong-placement and darkness field explains why this refrain ends here with injustice after 5:44 named denial and 5:47 names defiance.
words.root_gloss_range: wrongdoing, injustice, putting something out of place, and darkness; locally the class verdict for refusing revealed judgment

topics.headline: wrongdoers seal the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees refusal to judge by revelation interpreted as injustice and misplacement, not merely procedural failure.
topics.reason: The definite plural active participle completes the verdict; z-l-m rows preserve wrong-placement and darkness, while the triad with 5:44 and 5:47 frames this as the wrongdoing angle on the same refusal.
